management_steps.details: Body part bitten, time of bite, description of the snake if known, signs and symptoms (severe pain, headache, dizziness, dry mouth, severe thirst, nausea/vomiting, increased/severe sweating, limbs feeling weak, breathless, bitter taste in mouth). Ask about previous snakebites, prior antivenom treatment, and prior anaphylaxis to antivenom.

PPS/PW syndrome (mixed cytotoxic & neurotoxic, e.g. Mozambique spitting cobra): painful progressive swelling and progressive weakening. PPS syndrome (cytotoxic, e.g. puff adder, Gaboon viper, rinkhals, berg adder): local swelling, may need surgical review. PW syndrome (neurotoxic, e.g. black/green mamba, non-spitting cobra): progressive weakening, ptosis, difficulty swallowing, respiratory paralysis — protect airway. B syndrome (haemotoxic, e.g. boomslang, vine snake): bleeding, fang punctures that do not stop bleeding, use the 20-minute whole blood clotting test.

Take a few millilitres of blood by venepuncture into a new, clean, dry glass vessel. Leave undisturbed at room temperature for 20 minutes, then tilt once to see if the blood has clotted. If blood remains incoagulable 6 hours after the first antivenom dose, repeat the dose until coagulability is restored.

Insert an IV line (not in the same limb as the bite). Doctor to administer antivenom; no test dose required. Diluted 50/50 in isotonic fluid infused over 15-30 minutes, EXCEPT boomslang/vine snake monovalent antivenom which is given as a slow IV push (1 ampoule/min). Indicative starting doses: rinkhals 50ml; puff adder/spitting cobras/Gaboon adder 50-200ml depending on species; other species (mamba, non-spitting cobra) per polyvalent protocol; boomslang/vine snake 20ml monovalent. Monitor swelling hourly, neurological symptoms closely, and repeat the clotting test as needed.

If any allergy screen answer is positive (medication allergy, prior antivenom, asthma/hay fever, infantile eczema, other allergies, prior snakebite), prepare for a high possibility of anaphylaxis: give IM adrenaline 15 minutes prior to antivenom (weight/age-based dosing, e.g. 1-3 years <11kg: 0.10mg IM). Monitor closely during antivenom infusion for shortness of breath, laryngeal swelling, bronchospasm, cyanosis, or cardiovascular collapse.

warnings: Do NOT apply a tourniquet, incise the wound, or attempt suction.
Natal black snake / stiletto snake bites cause local damage only and require conservative management — no antivenom; consult the Snakebite Advisory group before any digit amputation.
Antivenom carries a real risk of anaphylaxis — always prepare resuscitation equipment, adrenaline, and antihistamines beforehand.
